The carriage stopped at last before a gate overgrown with ivy, and Anne climbed down with her carpetbag clutched in both hands. The evening was soft and gold, and the road behind her was lined with trees in bloom, like white arms stretched toward the sky. “It’s so beautiful,” she whispered. “I never imagined a place could be so beautiful.” The driver, who was not accustomed to such remarks, grunted and busied himself with the reins. But Anne had stopped listening; she was staring at the long path to the house, where a lamp had just been lit in an upstairs window, and her heart was beating so fast she was afraid it might be heard.
